top_limitations.limitation: Popularity is a historical Spotify platform proxy and the dataset is temporally and contextually limited.
top_limitations.impact: The target is not musical quality or guaranteed commercial success; marketing, artist fame, playlists and newer market behavior are not represented by the 18 baseline inputs.
top_limitations.mitigation_current: Temporal split, time-slice evaluation, explicit estimate wording and responsible-use disclosure.
top_limitations.future_improvement: Acquire newer time-stamped data, define a prediction-time target, and add leakage-safe contextual features available at release time.

top_limitations.limitation: Predictive generalization is weak and degrades on the later held-out test period.
top_limitations.impact: Test MAE is 17.65, RMSE 21.01 and R2 0.0696; validation-to-test RMSE rises 37.77%, so individual errors can be large and later data is harder.
top_limitations.mitigation_current: Report test and slice metrics, retain underprediction warning, avoid guarantees, and keep the system as a research prototype.
top_limitations.future_improvement: Study drift, recalibrate/retrain on newer data under a new version, add richer features, and compare against updated baselines without opening the locked test set for tuning.

top_limitations.limitation: SHAP and What-if explain model behavior, not real-world causal effects.
top_limitations.impact: A contribution or changed prediction cannot justify advice that altering an audio feature will make a song popular.
top_limitations.mitigation_current: Noncausal UI wording, claim audit, backend-only SHAP and offline NOT_AVAILABLE policy for Explain/What-if.
top_limitations.future_improvement: Add uncertainty/context displays and, for causal questions, design a separate causal study with explicit assumptions and intervention data.
